chapters.title: Linear Equations
chapters.summary: Solve equations of the form ax + b = c and read their graphs as straight lines.
chapters.html:
A linear equation is a statement that two expressions are equal, where the unknown appears only to the first power. Solving it means finding the value that makes the statement true.

The golden rule

Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you must do to the other. This keeps the equation balanced, like a set of scales.

ax + b = c  ⟹  x = (c − b) ÷ a

Worked example

Solve 2x + 5 = 17.

  1. Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 12
  2. Divide both sides by 2: x = 6
  3. Check: 2(6) + 5 = 17 ✓

Seeing equations as lines

Every linear equation in two variables, such as y = 2x + 1, draws a straight line. The number in front of x is the slope and the constant is the y-intercept.

Common equation shapes

EquationFirst stepAnswer
x + 7 = 12Subtract 7x = 5
3x = 21Divide by 3x = 7
x/4 = 2Multiply by 4x = 8
5x − 3 = 2x + 9Collect x termsx = 4

Watch out. When you move a term across the equals sign, its sign changes. Forgetting this is the most common mistake in exams.

Key takeaway. Undo operations in reverse order (add/subtract first, then multiply/divide) and always check your answer by substituting it back.

chapters.html:
Describe collections of objects as sets and place every number in the real number system.

Key ideas

  • A set can be written by listing (roster) or by a rule (set-builder notation).
  • Union (∪) joins sets; intersection (∩) keeps common elements.
  • Natural ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rationals ⊂ Reals; √2 and π are irrational.

chapters.title: Characteristics of Living Things
chapters.summary: Identify the features shared by every living organism.
chapters.html:
Every living organism, from a bacterium to a blue whale, shares the same set of life processes. Remember them with the word MRS GREN.

The seven life processes

LetterProcessMeaning
MMovementChanging position or moving parts
RRespirationReleasing energy from food
SSensitivityDetecting and responding to changes
GGrowthPermanent increase in size
RReproductionProducing offspring
EExcretionRemoving waste products
NNutritionTaking in or making food

Watch: growth and change

Insects such as butterflies change body form as they grow. This is called metamorphosis.

Demo clip. Replace with your own lesson video.

Exam tip. Fire and cars can move and “use fuel”, but they do not reproduce or grow by themselves, so they are not alive.

chapters.title: The Cell
chapters.summary: Explore the structure of plant and animal cells and what each organelle does.
chapters.html:
The cell is the basic unit of life. All organisms are made of one or more cells, and every cell comes from another cell.

Organelles and their jobs

  • Nucleus: contains DNA and controls the cell’s activities.
  • Mitochondria: release energy through respiration.
  • Ribosomes: build proteins.
  • Cell membrane: controls what enters and leaves.

Plant vs animal cells

StructurePlantAnimal
Cell wallYesNo
ChloroplastsYesNo
Large vacuoleYesNo
NucleusYesYes
“All living things are composed of cells and cell products.” (Cell theory, Schleiden and Schwann, 1839)

Key takeaway. Structure matches function: cells that need lots of energy, like muscle cells, contain many mitochondria.

chapters.title: Electric Circuits and Ohm's Law
chapters.summary: Relate voltage, current and resistance, and analyse simple circuits.
chapters.html:
Electric current is the flow of charge. Ohm’s law links the push that drives the current (voltage) with how hard the circuit resists it (resistance).

V = I × R

The three quantities

QuantitySymbolUnit
VoltageVvolt (V)
CurrentIampere (A)
ResistanceRohm (Ω)

Worked example

A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current.

  1. Write the law: I = V ÷ R
  2. Substitute: I = 12 ÷ 4
  3. Answer: I = 3 A

Series and parallel

  • Series: R = R₁ + R₂. The same current flows through each resistor.
  • Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂. The total resistance is smaller than either resistor.

Safety. Never connect an ammeter in parallel with a component: its very low resistance can draw a dangerous current.

chapters.title: The Mole Concept
chapters.summary: Count particles by weighing and use moles in calculations.
chapters.html:
Atoms are far too small to count one by one, so chemists count them in groups called moles. One mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro’s number).

n = m ÷ M

where n is the amount in moles, m is the mass in grams and M is the molar mass in g/mol.

Molar masses to know

SubstanceFormulaM (g/mol)
WaterH₂O18
Carbon dioxideCO₂44
Sodium chlorideNaCl58.5
GlucoseC₆H₁₂O₆180

Worked example

How many moles are in 88 g of CO₂?

  1. Molar mass: 12 + 2 × 16 = 44 g/mol
  2. n = 88 ÷ 44
  3. Answer: 2 mol, or 1.20 × 10²⁴ molecules

Memory trick. Cover the quantity you want in the triangle m over n × M, and the remaining two show you the calculation.

Key takeaway. The mole is the bridge between the mass you can weigh and the number of particles that react.

chapters.title: Differentiation
chapters.summary: Find rates of change and the slopes of curves.
chapters.html:
Differentiation finds the instantaneous rate of change of a function, which is the slope of the tangent line to its graph at any point.

f′(x) = limh→0 [f(x + h) − f(x)] ÷ h

Rules you will use most

FunctionDerivative
c (constant)0
xⁿn·xⁿ⁻¹
sin xcos x
eˣeˣ
ln x1/x

Worked example

Differentiate f(x) = 3x⁴ − 5x² + 7.

  1. Apply the power rule term by term.
  2. 3 · 4x³ − 5 · 2x + 0
  3. Answer: f′(x) = 12x³ − 10x

Where derivatives are zero

At a maximum or minimum the tangent is horizontal, so f′(x) = 0. Solving this equation is how you optimise areas, costs and profits in exam problems.

Key takeaway. A derivative is a slope. Positive means increasing, negative means decreasing, and zero marks a turning point.

questions.text: Solve for x: 2x + 5 = 17
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 12, then divide by 2: x = 6.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: What are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor the quadratic: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If log₁₀ x = 3, what is x?
questions.explanation: log₁₀ x = 3 means 10³ = x, so x = 1000.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180° = 4 × 180° = 720°.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: What is the value of sin 30°?
questions.explanation: In a 30-60-90 triangle the side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse, so sin 30° = 1/2.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: In the arithmetic sequence 3, 7, 11, …, what is the 10th term?
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: What is the derivative of f(x) = x³?
questions.explanation: By the power rule, d/dx xⁿ = n·xⁿ⁻¹, so d/dx x³ = 3x².
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Evaluate ∫ 2x dx.
questions.explanation: The antiderivative of 2x is x², plus a constant C.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.explanation: There are 6 favourable outcomes (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1) out of 36, so P = 6/36 = 1/6.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Evaluate lim (x→2) (x² − 4)/(x − 2).
questions.explanation: (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2, so the limit is 2 + 2 = 4.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N), where 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What is its final velocity?
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law, I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg mass moving at 3 m/s?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of these quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others are scalars.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the period of a wave with a frequency of 50 Hz?
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the equivalent resistance of 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors connected in parallel?
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An object is dropped from rest and falls for 3 s. How far does it fall? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: s = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 3² = 45 m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the atomic number of carbon?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25 °C?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: What is the molar mass of water (H₂O)?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: What type of bond holds sodium chloride (NaCl) together?
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by an ionic bond.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: How many moles are in 44 g of carbon dioxide (CO₂)?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂, so hydrogen gas is released.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: What is the oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: K is +1 and each O is −2: 1 + x − 8 = 0, so x = +7.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell’s ATP through cellular respiration.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Where does photosynthesis take place in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In DNA, adenine pairs with which base?
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G pairs with C. Uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In a cross Aa × Aa, what fraction of offspring show the recessive phenotype?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1, so 1/4 are aa.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which blood cells mainly fight infection?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leukocytes) are part of the immune system.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which type of cell division produces gametes?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number to produce haploid gametes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: “She ___ to school every day.”
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subjects take -s in the simple present: “she goes”.
questions.subject: English

questions.text: Which word is a synonym of “abundant”?
questions.explanation: “Abundant” means existing in large quantities: plentiful.
questions.subject: English

questions.text: Choose the passive form of “The teacher marked the papers.”
options: The papers was marked by the teacher.
The papers were marked by the teacher.
The teacher was marked by the papers.
The papers are marking by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The plural subject “papers” takes “were”, followed by the past participle “marked”.
questions.subject: English

questions.text: Which word is the opposite of “ancient”?
questions.explanation: “Ancient” means very old, so its antonym is “modern”.
questions.subject: English

questions.text: Complete the sentence: “If I ___ you, I would study harder.”
questions.explanation: Hypothetical (second) conditionals use “were” for all subjects.
questions.subject: English
